questions.question: What is the coefficient of expansion of brass when exposed to changes in temperature?
options: Has a negligible coefficient of linear expansion
Is not affected by temperature changes
questions.explanation: Brass has a relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion compared to other metals like invar, which is why it is often used in bimetallic strips.

questions.question: Which instrument provides the pilot with attitude information without external visual reference?
questions.explanation: The Attitude Indicator (Artificial Horizon) uses a gyroscope to display pitch and roll relative to the Earth's horizon.

questions.question: Static pressure is fed into which of the following flight instruments?
options: Altimeter, Airspeed Indicator, and Vertical Speed Indicator
questions.explanation: Static pressure is used by all three pitot-static instruments: the Altimeter, Airspeed Indicator, and Vertical Speed Indicator.

questions.question: In an aircraft pitot-static system, what happens to the airspeed indicator if the pitot tube drain and ram air hole freeze shut during climb?
options: It acts like an altimeter and indicates increasing airspeed
It freezes at the last indicated airspeed
It oscillates rapidly between high and low values
questions.explanation: Trapped air in the pitot chamber will act like an aneroid barometer, causing the airspeed indicator to read higher as ambient static pressure decreases during a climb.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a Bourdon tube in aircraft instrumentation?
options: To measure high fluid or gas pressures such as hydraulic or oil pressure
To measure electrical voltage of the alternator
questions.explanation: A Bourdon tube is a curved, hollow metal tube that straightens under pressure, commonly used in high-pressure oil and hydraulic gauges.

questions.question: A thermocouple temperature sensor operates based on which physical principle?
questions.explanation: Thermocouples work via the Seebeck effect: two dissimilar metals joined together produce a voltage proportional to temperature difference.

questions.question: What type of gyro is utilized in an aircraft turn coordinator?
options: Rate gyro with its gimbal tilted at approximately 30 degrees
Tied gyro with north-seeking slave unit
questions.explanation: A turn coordinator uses a rate gyro canted at about 30 degrees so that it senses both rate of roll and rate of yaw.

questions.question: Which of the following errors is characteristic of a magnetic compass during acceleration on an east or west heading in the Northern Hemisphere?
options: No error occurs on east or west headings
questions.explanation: ANDS rule: Accelerate North, Decelerate South when flying on easterly or westerly headings in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.question: What is the calibrated airspeed (CAS) corrected for to obtain true airspeed (TAS)?
questions.explanation: True Airspeed is Calibrated Airspeed corrected for altitude and non-standard temperature (air density variations).

questions.question: What does the green arc on an airspeed indicator represent?
questions.explanation: The green arc indicates the normal operating range of the aircraft from Vs1 (stall speed clean) to Vno (maximum structural cruising speed).

questions.question: Which instrument detects the rate of change in static pressure to indicate climb or descent rate?
questions.explanation: The VSI utilizes a calibrated leak orifice to measure the differential pressure between inside and outside of an aneroid capsule as static pressure changes.

questions.question: What is the function of a flux valve (flux gate) in a slaved directional gyro system?
options: To detect the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field
To cancel centrifugal force during turns
questions.explanation: A flux valve senses the direction of the Earth's horizontal magnetic flux lines and sends correction signals to continuously slave the gyro.

questions.question: What does an Electronic Flight Instrument System (EFIS) PFD primarily display?
options: Navigation maps and terrain radar only
Primary flight dynamics: attitude, airspeed, altitude, heading, and vertical speed
Electrical bus distribution and circuit breaker status
questions.explanation: The Primary Flight Display (PFD) consolidates the six core flight instruments into a single comprehensive glass screen.

questions.question: If an aircraft altimeter subscale is set to 29.92 inHg (1013.25 hPa), what altitude does it indicate?
questions.explanation: Setting standard sea level pressure 29.92 inHg on the Kollsman window causes the altimeter to indicate Pressure Altitude.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an accelerometer (g-meter) on high-performance aircraft?
options: To measure ground speed along the runway
To record structural load factors along the vertical aircraft axis
questions.explanation: Accelerometers record the positive and negative g-forces acting perpendicularly on the aircraft airframe during maneuvers or turbulence.

questions.question: What are the four strokes of a reciprocating internal combustion engine in order?
options: D. Fuel delivery, compression, expansion, scavenge
questions.explanation: The four-stroke Otto cycle sequence is intake, compression, power, and exhaust.

questions.question: What is the primary function of an aircraft engine turbocharger?
options: A. To cool cylinder head temperatures
B. To maintain sea-level manifold pressure at higher altitudes
C. To directly drive the propeller gearbox
D. To vaporize fuel before entering the cylinders
questions.explanation: A turbocharger maintains sea-level rated manifold pressure as ambient atmospheric pressure falls with increasing altitude.

questions.question: In a gas turbine engine, which section experiences the highest gas temperatures?
options: C. Turbine inlet guide vanes and first-stage turbine nozzle
questions.explanation: The turbine nozzle and first-stage turbine guide vanes bear the extreme hot combustion gas directly from the combustor.

questions.question: The VSV position during engine start-up is:
questions.explanation: During engine start-up, the Variable Stator Vanes (VSV) are in the fully closed position to provide high pressure ratio and stable airflow through the compressor.

questions.question: What causes magneto timing drift in piston aero engines?
options: A. Breaker point contact wear and cam follower wear
questions.explanation: Breaker point contact erosion and rubbing block/cam follower wear are the main causes of internal timing drift in aircraft magnetos.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of twin magnetos in an aircraft piston engine?
options: A. To charge dual 24V batteries simultaneously
B. Redundancy for safety and more complete fuel combustion via dual spark plugs
C. One operates cylinders 1-3 and the other operates 4-6
D. To provide electrical power to cockpit avionics
questions.explanation: Dual magnetos offer dual redundancy if one fails, and two spark plugs per cylinder yield more complete, faster combustion.

questions.question: What is the function of a deaerator?
options: A. Removes air and gases from fuel and lubricating oil systems
B. Increases engine bleed air pressure for anti-icing
C. Cools hydraulic fluid prior to pump intake
questions.explanation: A deaerator separates entrapped air bubbles and volatile vapor from fuel or lubricating engine oil, preventing pump cavitation and foaming.

questions.question: Which component regulates fuel flow in a modern commercial turbofan engine?
options: B. Hydro-mechanical unit (HMU) commanded by FADEC/EEC
questions.explanation: The Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) commands the Hydro-Mechanical Unit (HMU) torque motor to precisely meter fuel flow.

questions.question: Which structural member in a semi-monocoque fuselage carries the primary bending loads?
questions.explanation: Longerons are heavy longitudinal members that absorb and transfer principal bending loads in a semi-monocoque fuselage.

questions.question: What is the primary hazard of intergranular corrosion in aluminum airframe alloys?
options: A. It only discolors the exterior paint coating
B. It forms along the grain boundaries unseen from the surface and causes sudden structural failure
D. It increases electrical resistance of static wicks
questions.explanation: Intergranular corrosion attacks the grain boundaries inside high-strength aluminum alloys, weakening structure without noticeable exterior clues.

questions.question: What aerodynamic control surface controls aircraft yaw?
questions.explanation: The rudder is hinged to the vertical stabilizer and controls aircraft motion about the vertical axis (yaw).

questions.question: What is the purpose of vortex generators mounted along the upper surface of a wing?
options: A. To increase cruising speed by 20%
B. To delay boundary layer separation and prevent stall at high angles of attack
C. To generate lift while parked on the ground
D. To dump lift during landing rollout
questions.explanation: Vortex generators energize the boundary layer by mixing high-energy air downward, delaying aerodynamic stall.

questions.question: Which type of hydraulic fluid is synthetic, fire-resistant, and colored purple?
questions.explanation: Skydrol is a phosphate ester-based synthetic hydraulic fluid with extreme fire resistance, dyed purple for identification.
